Problem: -Woverflow warning caused by HAL CRC function
Context: repo=STM32CubeF0, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=17

Fix: Hello, this warning started showing recently when I build my project: .
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, bug_report, high, internal bug tracker, cmsis, IDR, CLEAR_REG, CRC

Technical details:
Hello, this warning started showing recently when I build my project: ../Drivers/CMSIS/Device/ST/STM32F0xx/Include/stm32f0xx.h:198:41: warning: overflow in conversion from 'int' to 'uint8_t' {aka 'volatile unsigned char'} changes value from '(int)hcrc->Instance->IDR & -256' to '0' [-Woverflow] The offending line is here in the de-init function: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF0/blob/830a0e950d421c17abff57a2ea1e977870355519/Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_crc.c#L205 I have two suggestions for fixes: 1. Use instead the macro from stm32f0xx.h CLEAR_REG(hcrc->Instance->IDR); 2. Use instead the macro from the CRC header file __HAL_CRC_SET_IDR(hcrc, 0); I'll leave it to you to select the best fix as I may not be aware of any knock-on effects. I would very much appreciate if this change could be made, since I usually aim for 0 errors and 0 warnings for any released firmware and this warning is the only one I have currently. With it being in the driver code I cannot simply make the change myself.

issues.issue_title: Missing ";" in cmsis_os.h, FreeRTOS - CMSIS V1.11.x
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Missing ";" in cmsis_os.h, FreeRTOS - CMSIS V1.11.x
Context: repo=STM32CubeF0, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=FREERTOS, layer=Middleware, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=high, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=14
Root cause: Hi @therocketelectrician, Thank you for this report.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** Programming a STM32F072B With STM32CubeIDE Version: 1.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: Middleware, FREERTOS, usage_question, high, invalid, cube mx, mw, cmsis, STM32F072B, UTC, STM32, RC5

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** Programming a STM32F072B With STM32CubeIDE Version: 1.7.0 Build: 10852_20210715_0634 (UTC) and STM32CubeMX - STM32 Device Configuration Tool Version: 6.3.0-RC5 Build: 20210714-1111 (UTC) **Describe the bug** I get this build error: C:/Users/User/STM32Cube/Repository/STM32Cube_FW_F0_V1.11.3/Middlewares/Third_Party/FreeRTOS/Source/CMSIS_RTOS/cmsis_os.h:825:1: error: expected ';' before 'extern' 825 | extern osMailQDef_t os_mailQ_def_##name **How To Reproduce** 1.1 Create a FreeRTOS project for a STM32F072B with the FreeRTOS API-CMSIS V1 1.2 Create an osMailQDef(writeAnalog_mail, 2, analogData_t); in the main.h 1.3 In main.c, put that code: #define osObjectsExternal #include "main.h" main(){ writeAnalog_mail = osMailCreate(osMailQ(writeAnalog_mail), NULL); } 2. The modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem (Driver, BSP, MW ...). In the file name is : "cmsis_os.h". // ==== Mail Queue Management Functions ==== #if (defined (osFeature_MailQ) && (osFeature_MailQ != 0)) // Mail Queues available /// \brief Create a Mail Queue Definition. /// \param name name of the queue /// \param queue_sz maximum number of messages in queue /// \param type data type of a single message element /// \note CAN BE CHANGED: The parameter to \b osMailQDef shall be consistent but the /// macro body is implementation specific in every CMSIS-RTOS. #if defined (osObjectsExternal) // object is external #define osMailQDef(name, queue_sz, type) \ extern struct os_mailQ_cb *os_mailQ_cb_##name \ extern osMailQDef_t os_mailQ_def_##name #else // define the object #define osMailQDef(name, queue_sz, type) \ struct os_mailQ_cb *os_mailQ_cb_##name \ const osMailQDef_t os_mailQ_def_##name = \ { (queue_sz), sizeof (type), (&os_mailQ_cb_##name) } #endif 3. The use case that generates the problem. Write what is explained in "1" and simply build. An error should appear. The way to solve it, which worked for me was to add ';' at the end of extern struct os_mailQ_cb *os_mailQ_cb_##name, extern osMailQDef_t os_mailQ_def_##name, struct os_mailQ_cb *os_mailQ_cb_##name, const osMailQDef_t os_mailQ_def_##name = { (queue_sz), sizeof (type), (&os_mailQ_cb_##name)} , The end result should look like this: #if defined (osObjectsExternal) // object is external #define osMailQDef(name, queue_sz, type) \ extern struct os_mailQ_cb *os_mailQ_cb_##name; \ extern osMailQDef_t os_mailQ_def_##name; #else // define the object #define osMailQDef(name, queue_sz, type) \ struct os_mailQ_cb *os_mailQ_cb_##name; \ const osMailQDef_t os_mailQ_def_##name = \ { (queue_sz), sizeof (type), (&os_mailQ_cb_##name) } ; #endif **Additional context** Maybe look and test all "extern" definition if there is any ";" missing.

Key comments:
Hi @therocketelectrician, Thank you for this report. We will get back to you with a feedback as soon as possible. Please excuse the delay it may take us sometimes to reply. Thank you for your comprehension. Hi @therocketelectrician, First we would like to thank you for your report. We tried to reproduce the issue you have described using the STM32CubeMX v6.5.A13 and the IAR v8.50.6 running on STM32F072RB board, with no success. I really hope you could find the root cause of this problem and, ideally, solve it. Regarding the point for which you opened the issue, as it is irrelevant, allow me to close the issue. Anyway, if you ever become able to reproduce systematically the faulty behavior and find out that the problem is related to our drivers, do not hesitate to recontract me. We could reopen this issue again. Thank you for your comprehension and thank you again for your report. We are looking forward to reading from you again.

Problem: Including `stm32f0xx_ll_adc.h` introduces ` `-Wunused-parameter` warnings into client code
Context: repo=STM32CubeF0, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=ADC, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=12
Root cause: Hi @mayl, Thank you for your contribution.
Fix: The offending section is below: https://github.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, ADC, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker

Technical details:
The offending section is below: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF0/blob/4390ff6bfb693104cf97192f98c3dc9e3a7c296a/Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32f0xx_ll_adc.h#L1411-L1415 The parameter Register is not used. However, because this is a function body defined in a header file, any _users_ of this library wind up hitting compiler warnings for this oversight. I build my projects with -Werror, and so this becomes an error for me. I don't know for sure what the project's preferred fix is but a couple that come to mind (some could work in combination): * Don't define the body of this function in the header file * Eliminate this unnecessary Register argument from the function definition * Add a (void) Register; line to the function to appease the compiler and eliminate the warning Thanks for your consideration

Problem: Race condition in HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_Start()
Context: repo=STM32CubeF0, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=ADC, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=10
Root cause: Hi @pmacfarlane A similar issue on HAL ADC has been identified on another STM32 series: small internal timeout checks are vulnerable to race condition and a correction is under study.
Fix: This problem was seen on an STM32F030 but I imagine would be seen on any similar MCU using the HAL.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, ADC, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, spotted before customer, STM32F030, MCU, HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_Start, HAL_GetTick, HAL_IS_BIT_SET

Technical details:
This problem was seen on an STM32F030 but I imagine would be seen on any similar MCU using the HAL. Sometimes, calls to HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_Start() will fail. This is especially true if you set the tick frequency to 100Hz or less. The issue is here: tickstart = HAL_GetTick(); /* Wait for calibration completion */ while(HAL_IS_BIT_SET(hadc->Instance->CR, ADC_CR_ADCAL)) { if((HAL_GetTick() - tickstart) > ADC_CALIBRATION_TIMEOUT) If we get a tick interrupt immediately after the first call to HAL_GetTick(), this adds 10 to the tick value (assuming a 100Hz tick). We then immediately timeout and return a failure. This problem may (or may not) also exist in the HAL libraries for other MCUs.

Key comments:
Hi @pmacfarlane A similar issue on HAL ADC has been identified on another STM32 series: small internal timeout checks are vulnerable to race condition and a correction is under study. Regards ST Internal Reference: 100410

Keywords: CAN, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, cmsis, FM1R, FBM27, RM0091, FBM0, FBM13, FS1R

Technical details:
Hi, looking at https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF0/blob/4390ff6bfb693104cf97192f98c3dc9e3a7c296a/Drivers/CMSIS/Device/ST/STM32F0xx/Include/stm32f042x6.h#L1580 it seems the bxCAN FM1R register has bits defined up to FBM27, but the ref manual RM0091 only lists FBM0..FBM13 . Seems to be the same situation for other filter registers (FS1R, FFA1R..) Is there a reason for this apparent doubling of bit defines ? issues.issue_title: HAL I2C OA1EN always set even when slave is not used
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: HAL I2C OA1EN always set even when slave is not used
Context: repo=STM32CubeF0, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=configuration_help, severity=medium, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=7
Root cause: Hi @eelmor, Thank you for your report.
Fix: Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_i2c.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, configuration_help, medium, needs clarification, OAR1, HAL_I2C_Init

Technical details:
Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_i2c.c /*---------------------------- I2Cx OAR1 Configuration ---------------------*/ /* Disable Own Address1 before set the Own Address1 configuration */ hi2c->Instance->OAR1 &= ~I2C_OAR1_OA1EN; /* Configure I2Cx: Own Address1 and ack own address1 mode */ if (hi2c->Init.AddressingMode == I2C_ADDRESSINGMODE_7BIT) { hi2c->Instance->OAR1 = (I2C_OAR1_OA1EN | hi2c->Init.OwnAddress1); } else /* I2C_ADDRESSINGMODE_10BIT */ { hi2c->Instance->OAR1 = (I2C_OAR1_OA1EN | I2C_OAR1_OA1MODE | hi2c->Init.OwnAddress1); I2C_OAR1_OA1EN is always set in HAL_I2C_Init which is causing issues in multi-master situations. The I2C driver will address match (address 0 if not configured) even when only used in Master-mode causing a stall on the bus if not handled separately in user-code.

Key comments:
Hi @eelmor, Thank you for your report. It has been forwarded to our development teams. We will get back to you as soon as they provide us with their feedback. Hi @eelmor, Sorry for the delay in coming back to you. Your request has been forwarded to our development team and they are asking for more clarification about the multi-master use. Please allow me then to ask you few questions : - As the Address “0” is reserved to general call, please make sure that you have configured a correct (real) address. - Are you using our MCU as master with another MCU (2 MCUs used) ? Or are you using only one MCU and declaring different I2C instances as masters within your application ? Hello @ASELSTM, 1. I'm not sure about the exact matching criteria as I don't know the exact data being sent by the other master, but the I2C_ISR ADDR bit keeps getting set when using the I2C peripheral in Master mode which stalls the peripheral. I don't see any reason to set the OA1EN bit when used as Master only. 2. Yes, two masters on the I2C bus (2x MCU). Hi @eelmor, Referring to your feedback, the behavior you are detecting means that you didn't set an own address value on the initialization phase.

Problem: Fault in HAL_CEC code
Context: repo=STM32CubeF0, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=5
Root cause: Hi @newbrain, Thank you for this report.
Fix: **Problem Location:** stm32f0xx_hal_cec.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, ISR, CEC, STM32, STM32F7, TECH037361, HAL_CEC_Transmit_IT, EOM

Technical details:
**Problem Location:** stm32f0xx_hal_cec.c file in ./Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Src. **Problem:** The _HAL_CEC_Transmit_IT()_ function, in conjunction with the _HAL_CEC_IRQHandler()_ ISR will always append an extra byte to the end of message, unless only one byte (header only: CEC ping) is sent. This will cause many TVs to ignore the whole message (some might work, e.g. some recent Sony). The problem has been confirmed with TVs from Sony, LG, Samsung and other brands, with models of varied vintage and checked with an oscilloscope. The proposed solution has been verified in the same way. **Note: This is the third time I report this fault, that affects also the libraries for other STM32 models with CEC, e.g. STM32F7.** First report: TECH037361 or CTNbg19058 (2017) Second report: Case# 00082897 (2019) Both times the fault was acknowledged (as was the proposed solution) and said to be corrected in a next version. **Root Cause:** When a single byte (i.e. a CEC header) is to be transmitted, HAL_CEC_Transmit_IT() correctly sets the EOM bit: /* in case of no payload (Size = 0), sender is only pinging the system; Set TX End of Message (TXEOM) bit, must be set before writing data to TXDR */ if (Size == 0U) { __HAL_CEC_LAST_BYTE_TX_SET(hcec); } HAL_CEC_IRQHandler() will then just clean up and invoke the TX complete callback. When any payload needs to be transmitted (Size > 0), its size will be assigned to TxXferCount: /* initialize the number of bytes to send, * 0 means only one header is sent (ping operation) */ hcec->TxXferCount = Size; In the IRS, when a TXBR interrupt is being served and the last byte is about to be sent, TxXferCount will still be 1: /* CEC TX byte request interrupt ------------------------------------------------*/ if((reg & CEC_FLAG_TXBR) != RESET) { if (hcec->TxXferCount == 0U) { /* if this is the last byte transmission, set TX End of Message (TXEOM) bit */ __HAL_CEC_LAST_BYTE_TX_SET(hcec); hcec->Instance->TXDR = *hcec->pTxBuffPtr; hcec->pTxBuffPtr++; } else { hcec->Instance->TXDR = *hcec->pTxBuffPtr; hcec->pTxBuffPtr++; hcec->TxXferCount--; } /* clear Tx-Byte request flag */ __HAL_CEC_CLEAR_FLAG(hcec,CEC_FLAG_TXBR); } The check for TxXferCount is the source of the error: when the last byte is going to be transmitted, TxXferCount is still 1, not 0, as it's decremented only after writing TXDR; for this reason, the TXBR interrupt will be invoked one additional time (possibly reading past the end of the transmit buffer!) and an unknown value will be appended to the message. **Solution:** Correct the check for the last message byte in HAL_CEC_IRQHandler(): /* CEC TX byte request interrupt ------------------------------------------------*/ if((reg & CEC_FLAG_TXBR) != RESET) { if (--hcec->TxXferCount == 0U) /* pre-decrement the size before the comparison */ { /* if this is the last byte transmission, set TX End of Message (TXEOM) bit */ __HAL_CEC_LAST_BYTE_TX_SET(hcec); } /* In all cases transmit the byte */ hcec->Instance->TXDR = *hcec->pTxBuffPtr++; /* clear Tx-Byte request flag */ __HAL_CEC_CLEAR_FLAG(hcec,CEC_FLAG_TXBR); } **How to reproduce:** Just send any CEC message with a payload.

Thank you for your patience and thank you again for your contribution. Hi @newbrain, As promised we have reported your report to our development teams and they confirmed the issue. A fix will be implemented and made available in future release. Thank you once again for your contribution. ST Internal Reference: 87112 Hi @newbrain, I hope you are fine. The issue you reported has been fixed in the frame of version **v1.11.2** of the STM32CubeF0 published recently on GitHub. Thank you again for having reported.

issues.issue_title: UART ISR becomes interrupt bound due to incomplete implemenation of UART Recieve Timeout
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: UART ISR becomes interrupt bound due to incomplete implemenation of UART Recieve Timeout
Context: repo=STM32CubeF0, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=UART, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=4
Root cause: Hi David-oz00, Thank you for reporting this issue.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** * Hardware: Proprietary hardware containing STM32F030RC * IDE: VisualGDB with GCC 9.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, UART, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, STM32F030RC, IDE, GCC, ISR, BSP, HAL_UART_IRQHandler

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** * Hardware: Proprietary hardware containing STM32F030RC * IDE: VisualGDB with GCC 9.2.1 * HAL: 1.11.0 **Describe the bug** When the UART receive timeout is enabled, it is possible the ISR executes without clearing the interrupt. Consequently, the ISR is continuously called using 100% of the microprocessor time. **How To Reproduce** 1. Indicate the global behavior of your application project. A serial connection which uses intercharacter timeout to indicate the end of message. 2. The modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem (Driver, BSP, MW ...). HAL_UART_IRQHandler() ISR function in stm32f0xx_hal_uart.c 3. The use case that generates the problem. A serial connection that uses intercharacter timeout to detect 'end of message'. The receive timeout is enabled using the following functions: HAL_UART_ReceiverTimeout_Config(mHuart, mBitsPerCharacter); HAL_UART_EnableReceiverTimeout(mHuart); SET_BIT(mHuart->Instance->CR1, USART_CR1_RTOIE); // See Note Note: The receive timeout interrupt has to be enabled manually 4. How we can reproduce the problem. You need to generate a receive timeout interrupt and ensure no other UART interrupts are pending. Following this condition the ISR will become interrupt bound. **Additional context** The defect is in the ISR function HAL_UART_IRQHandler(). The following code: if ((errorflags != 0U) && (((cr3its & USART_CR3_EIE) != 0U) || ((cr1its & (USART_CR1_RXNEIE | USART_CR1_PEIE)) != 0U))) should be: if ((errorflags != 0U) && (((cr3its & USART_CR3_EIE) != 0U) || ((cr1its & (USART_CR1_RXNEIE | USART_CR1_PEIE | USART_CR1_RTOIE)) != 0U))) Notice **USART_CR1_RTOIE** is not present in the original code. When this is fixed, can you also integrate the enabling and disabling of the receive timeout interrupt into the HAL so it doesn't have to be done manually. **Screenshots** None

The issue you reported has been fixed in the frame of version **v1.11.2** of the STM32CubeF0 published recently on GitHub. Thank you again for having reported.

Problem: Conflicting types for 'assert_failed'
Context: repo=STM32CubeF0, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=high, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=3
Root cause: Hi David, As said in a previous [comment](https://github.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** Hardware: Proprietary hardware containing STM32F030RCTx.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, usage_question, high, wontfix, cube mx, IDE, GCC, USE_FULL_ASSERT, assert_failed, BSP

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** Hardware: Proprietary hardware containing STM32F030RCTx. IDE: VisualGDB with GCC 9.2.1 **Describe the bug** When **USE_FULL_ASSERT** is enabled, STM32CubeMX generates this function in _main.c_: void assert_failed(char *file, uint32_t line) however the prototype in _stm32f0xx_hal_conf.h_ has been changed to this: void assert_failed(uint8_t* file, uint32_t line); This causes a compile error from GCC **"error: conflicting types for 'assert_failed'"** **How To Reproduce** 1. Indicate the global behavior of your application project The application uses STM32CubeMX built in assert mechanism. This defect occurs at compile time. 2. The modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem (Driver, BSP, MW ...) _stm32f0xx_hal_conf.h_ (which is generated from the _stm32f0xx_hal_conf_template.h_) has been updated with a new prototype, but the function body in _main.c_ has not been updated. 3. The use case that generates the problem Compiling the application. 4. How we can reproduce the problem - Create a project in STM32CubeMX using this mcu package. Ensure Enable Full Assert is ticked (Project Manager\Code Generator\Hal Settings). - Generate the code and compile the project. A compile error is generated as in the description above. **Additional context** It looks like someone updated the prototype but forgot to update the body. The funny thing is _**uint8_t***_ is not correct anyway. I think it should be changed to _**const char***_, or at least keep it at _**char***_ **Screenshots** None

Hi David, As said in a previous [comment](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/issues/23#issuecomment-582294946), aspects related to Cube MX tool are not handled at GitHub level. They are rather treated at **ST Community** level, precisely within the [Cube MX](https://community.st.com/s/topic/0TO0X000000BTr8WAG/stm32cubemx) dedicated section. Please, allow me to close this issue. Thank you for your comprehension.
